title: Codebase Audit
tagline: Find out what is wrong before it costs you a customer.
summary: A three to five day read of your codebase that ends in a written report and a walkthrough call. You learn exactly what is broken, what it would cost you, and what to do first.
problem: You cannot fix what you cannot see. An AI coding tool will happily produce an application that works on your laptop, passes your manual click-through, and ships to production with your database credentials sitting in the repository. Nothing warns you. The first signal is usually a customer, an invoice, or an outage.
whatWeDo: Read every file in the repository, including the git history, where secrets tend to hide after being deleted from the current version
Check for exposed credentials, API keys and tokens, in the code and in every commit that came before it
Map how authentication and authorisation actually work, and find the routes where they are enforced on the client instead of the server
Review the database schema, indexes, and every query on a user-facing path
Confirm whether backups exist, whether they run, and whether anyone has ever restored one
Audit dependencies for known vulnerabilities and for versions far enough behind that upgrading is itself a project
Check error handling: what happens when a call fails, and whether anyone finds out
Measure real load performance rather than local performance
Review the deployment path and whether a bad release can be rolled back
whatYouGet: A written report, typically fifteen to thirty pages, with a plain-language summary at the front
Every finding rated critical, high, medium or low, with what it would actually cost you if it went wrong
A prioritised fix list, ordered by risk rather than by effort
A one-hour walkthrough call where you can ask why about anything in it
A fixed-price quote for the stabilisation work, if you want it
whatsNotIncluded: We do not fix anything during the audit. Reading and changing at the same time is how findings get lost.
No new features, no design work, no redesign proposals
No penetration testing or formal security certification
timeline: 3 to 5 working days from repository access

process.title: Thirty-minute call
process.description: You tell us what the product does, who uses it, and what you are worried about. We tell you whether an audit is the right thing to buy.

process.title: NDA and read-only access
process.description: We sign a mutual NDA, then you grant read-only access to the repository. Nothing else, and no write permissions.

process.title: The read
process.description: Three to five days of reading the codebase, the history, the schema, and the deployment path.

process.title: Report and walkthrough
process.description: You get the written report, then an hour on a call going through it. What you do next is entirely your call.

seo.title: Codebase Audit
seo.description: A 3 to 5 day audit of your AI generated codebase. Written report, severity-rated findings, prioritised fix list, and a walkthrough call. From $250.

title: Stabilisation
tagline: Fix the things that can actually hurt you.
summary: One to three weeks of focused work closing the critical and high findings from the audit, so your application stops being one bad day away from a serious problem.
problem: A report tells you where the holes are. It does not close them. Most people who read an audit intend to act on it, then get pulled back into shipping features, and the critical findings are still open six months later. Stabilisation exists so that does not happen.
whatWeDo: Rotate every exposed credential and move secrets out of the repository into proper environment configuration
Purge secrets from git history where they were committed and later deleted
Move authorisation checks to the server on every route where they were only enforced in the browser
Set up automated database backups, then restore one to prove the backup is real
Add error tracking and uptime monitoring, wired to alert a human rather than a dashboard nobody opens
Upgrade dependencies with known vulnerabilities, in reviewable steps rather than one large jump
Add tests around the paths where a failure costs money: payment, authentication, data writes
Fix the queries and pages that are slow under real load
Put a deployment path in place that can be rolled back in one step
whatYouGet: Every critical and high finding from the audit closed, or explicitly deferred with your agreement and the reason written down
Working backups you have watched us restore
Monitoring and alerting that reaches a person
A documented deployment and rollback procedure
A short written handover explaining everything that changed and why
whatsNotIncluded: No new features. Stabilisation makes what exists safe; it does not extend it.
No full rewrite. If a rewrite is genuinely the right answer we tell you, and we tell you not to pay us for a patch instead.
No backfilling of a complete test suite
timeline: 1 to 3 weeks, quoted exactly after the audit

process.title: Fixed quote
process.description: Based on the audit findings, you get an exact price and an exact scope. No hourly billing, no surprises.

process.title: Access and branch
process.description: We take write access to a working branch. Your main branch is untouched until you approve a merge.

process.title: Work in reviewable pieces
process.description: Changes arrive as small pull requests you or your developer can read, not one enormous commit at the end.

process.title: Verify and hand over
process.description: We restore a backup in front of you, trigger a test alert, and walk you through the rollback. Then you get the written handover.

seo.title: Stabilisation
seo.description: One to three weeks closing the critical findings in your codebase: secrets rotated, backups working, monitoring live, rollback in place. From $600.

title: Monthly Maintenance
tagline: Someone is watching it, so you do not have to.
summary: A monthly retainer that keeps your application patched, monitored, backed up and answered for. You stop being the person who finds out from a customer.
problem: Stabilisation is a snapshot. Dependencies keep releasing security patches, providers keep deprecating things, certificates keep expiring, and a codebase nobody is watching drifts back towards the state the audit found. Maintenance is the difference between fixed once and staying fixed.
whatWeDo: Monitor uptime and errors continuously, and respond when something breaks rather than waiting for you to report it
Apply security patches and dependency updates on a regular cadence, tested before they ship
Verify backups actually restore, on a schedule, rather than trusting that they run
Watch performance and cost, and flag when a query or a provider bill starts trending the wrong way
Keep documentation current as things change
Send a monthly written report: what happened, what we changed, what we are watching
Be reachable when you have a question about your own system
whatYouGet: A named engineer who knows your codebase, not a ticket queue
Monthly written reports you can forward to an investor or a co-founder
Response commitments that match your tier
A system that gets slightly better every month instead of slightly worse
whatsNotIncluded: Feature development is quoted separately, though we do it for maintenance clients
No 24/7 on-call at the entry tiers. We tell you exactly what the response window is before you sign.
timeline: Rolling monthly, thirty days' notice to cancel

process.title: Monthly rhythm
process.description: Patching, backup restore tests, and a written report on a predictable schedule.

process.title: Respond
process.description: When something breaks, we are the ones who notice and the ones who fix it.

seo.title: Monthly Maintenance

title: Automation & AI Integration
tagline: Build on top of a foundation we already trust.
summary: Workflow automation and AI features built into an application we already maintain. Available to existing clients only, quoted per project.
problem: Adding an AI feature or an automated workflow to a system nobody has audited multiplies whatever is already wrong with it. A background job with unbounded retries against an unindexed table is a small feature and a large bill. We only do this work on codebases we know.
whatWeDo: Automate manual internal processes: reporting, data entry, reconciliation, notifications
Integrate language model features where they solve a real problem, with cost ceilings and sensible failure behaviour
Build and monitor background jobs and scheduled tasks that fail loudly rather than silently
Connect the third-party systems your operation already runs on
Instrument the whole thing so you can see what it is doing and what it is costing
whatYouGet: A working automation with monitoring and cost controls attached from day one
Documentation of what it does and how to turn it off
The same maintenance coverage as the rest of your system
whatsNotIncluded: Not available as a standalone engagement. We only build on codebases we already maintain.
No AI feature added because it is expected to be there. If it does not solve a problem, we say so.
No model training or data science work
startingPrice: Quoted per project, existing clients only

process.title: Scope against what exists

process.title: Fixed quote

process.title: Build with the brakes on
process.description: Cost ceilings, rate limits, retries with backoff and alerting are part of the build, not a later addition.

process.title: Fold into maintenance
process.description: Whatever we build becomes part of what we monitor and patch every month.
